job.style: a step-by-step explanation of a process

response.passage: When light travels from one transparent medium to another, it changes speed, causing it to bend at the interface between the two materials. This phenomenon, known as refraction, occurs whenever light crosses a boundary between different optical densities, not just when entering liquids. To calculate the position of images formed by lenses, we use the lens formula, which is 1/v - 1/u = 1/f. This differs from the mirror formula because of the negative sign. When solving these problems, we must follow the New Cartesian Sign Convention. According to this, the object distance 'u' is always taken as negative because the object is placed to the left of the optical center. Furthermore, the power of a lens is defined as the reciprocal of its focal length in meters. Therefore, a lens with a higher power has a shorter focal length, as power and focal length are inversely proportional. Finally, when a portion of a lens is covered, the entire image is still formed, though it becomes dimmer because less light passes through the lens. The image does not disappear or get cut off; rather, the intensity of the light reaching the screen is reduced, ensuring the full shape remains visible.
response.summary: Refraction occurs at the boundary of any two transparent media due to a change in light speed. Lenses follow specific sign conventions and mathematical formulas that differ from mirrors, and covering part of a lens reduces image brightness without removing parts of the image.
